# The Grande Arbor: A Home Designed to Support Multigenerational Living


Published On: September 16, 2026


•


4 min read


•


The Grande Arbor by Cavco


[Cavco Industries](https://www.cavcohomes.com/) introduced a[manufactured home](https://www.cavcohomes.com/find-a-floor-plan) that breaks new ground in construction and floor plan design. The Grande Arbor gives growing, blended and multigenerational families more flexibility in how they live together, with space designed to provide privacy without separating the household.


The Grande Arbor, part of Cavco’s exclusive[Studio Collection](https://www.cavcohomes.com/studio-collection) , is the first HUD-approved manufactured home built without a permanent steel chassis. It also introduces the double Grande suite, an innovative floor plan designed specifically for multigenerational living.


## **A Home Built for the Way Families Live Today**


The Grande Arbor is the first HUD-approved manufactured home built without a permanent chassis, offering homeowners more flexibility.


For decades, manufactured homes have been built to sit on top of permanent steel chassis. The chassis is the heavy-duty steel frame that forms the home’s structural base and enables transport. The Grande Arbor is the first HUD-approved manufactured home engineered to stand without a permanent steel chassis frame, meaning the home is set on the ground on a foundation like a site-built home — and that innovation opens a world of affordable housing opportunities for Americans.


A home built without a permanent chassis means:


- **Lower-profile installation** with no steps or ramps required at entry. The home is set on a ground-level foundation, like an onsite-built home.


- **Enhanced curb appeal.** The home beautifully blends more naturally into existing neighborhoods.


- **Manufactured homes can be placed in more areas** including urban and suburban areas that were harder to serve before.


- **A wider design range** , including multi-story construction and larger homes.


The Grande Arbor’s design is a genuine engineering milestone innovation within the[HUD Code](https://blog.cavcohomes.com/what-is-the-hud-code-for-manufactured-homes/) , and it’s already drawing attention from customers, home designers, retailers and policymakers.


## **The Double Grande Suite: Made for Multigenerational Living**


The Grande Arbor is designed to support multigenerational living. Blended family life is at an all-time high, with families living with grandparents or adult children all under the same roof.


More than 74 million Americans currently share a multigenerational household, and nearly one in five homes purchased in 2024 were bought specifically to support multigenerational living.


Rising housing costs, aging parents, adult kids moving back home: the reasons for multigenerational living vary, but most of today’s housing floor plans haven’t caught up with the trending housing need. The double Grande suite was built to support family needs. Rather than the home having a single primary bedroom paired with a smaller second bedroom, the Grande Arbor design divides the home into two symmetrical wings, positioned on opposite ends with a shared kitchen, dining and living space in the home’s center.


> “This floor plan was all about creating a space where both bedrooms feel like primary suites,” said **Saul Morales** , the floor plan designer for the Grande Arbor. “Each suite has its own bathroom, walk-in closet with storage and privacy, with the shared living areas bringing everyone together in the middle.”


Morales also recessed each bedroom wing about 12 inches from the exterior wall. It’s a detail he says most buyers won’t consciously notice – but they’ll “feel it, in the added architectural depth outside and the stronger sense of space inside.”

## **Who the Double Grande Suite Is Built to Support**


The layout solves a common challenge for multigenerational households: how can multiple people live together under one roof but still have their own personal space? This floor plan is purposefully designed for:


- Adult children who’ve moved back home


- Aging parents or in-laws desiring to live closer to family


- Two households sharing one roof without sharing a bathroom


- Couples who want equal, independent space


- Homeowners looking to rent the second suite for extra income


- Anyone who needs a private home office or flex suite


## **Two Innovative Firsts in One Innovative Home**


The Grande Arbor pairs an industry-first innovation below the floor with a layout built for how families want to live today. Together, they open up new possibilities for manufactured housing – in how a home can be designed and built, where it can be placed and, most importantly, how well it can serve the people who will call it home.
